card.name: Modifier before a legal or clinical noun
card.fires_on: Small modifiers such as a, well, equal, legal or initial that come right before an expected noun phrase. The setting is mostly legal text (refugee status, equal protection, court rulings) and sometimes clinical text.

modes.label: Legal phrase openers
modes.description: A or an adjective just before a legal concept such as fear of persecution, protection rights or a compelling interest.
modes.example: you must have a<< well>>-founded fear of persecution based on race,

modes.label: Article before a legal noun
modes.description: The word a before a legal noun like case, necessity or interest.
modes.example: You may also have<< a>> case against the manufacturer of the asbestos product

modes.label: Clinical adjective
modes.description: The word initial before presentation in a warning about bipolar disorder.
modes.example: A major depressive episode may be the<< initial>> presentation of bipolar disorder.

card.plain: It fires on a small word like a or initial that is waiting for a legal or medical noun to follow.
